pi.name: Bo Duan
pi.title: Associate Professor of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology
pi.bio: Bo Duan is an Associate Professor in the Department of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology at the University of Michigan, where he founded his laboratory in 2016. His lab investigates the development, organization, and function of neural circuits underlying somatosensory modalities such as pain, itch, touch, and temperature sensation. The group uses mouse genetics, histochemistry, neuroanatomical tracing, electrophysiology, in vivo imaging, and behavioral analyses.

lab_description: The Bo Duan lab studies how the nervous system perceives and processes somatosensory information, including temperature, touch, pain, and itch. The lab investigates the neural circuits that transmit and process these distinct sensory modalities in the spinal cord and brain, and how the modalities interact with one another. Current projects aim to identify the spinal neurons that transmit thermal versus mechanical pain, the spinal circuits for mechanical itch, the peripheral sensory inputs that drive pain and itch, and the descending pathways that modulate pain and itch. The lab combines mouse genetics, histochemistry, neuroanatomical tracing, electrophysiology, in vivo imaging, and behavioral analyses.

research_areas.title: Thermal vs. mechanical pain transmission
research_areas.summary: Identifying the spinal neurons responsible for transmitting different types of pain.

research_areas.title: Mechanical itch circuits
research_areas.summary: Identifying the spinal circuits and dedicated hair afferents that transmit mechanical itch signals.

research_areas.title: Peripheral inputs for pain and itch
research_areas.summary: Characterizing the peripheral sensory inputs that drive painful and itchy sensations, including dedicated skin-to-brain circuits for temperature sensation.

research_areas.title: Descending modulation of pain and itch
research_areas.summary: Dissecting the descending neural pathways that regulate pain and itch responses.

Victor received the Best Talk Award at the MCDB department retreat.

joining: One postdoctoral fellow position is available. Candidates should have a neuroscience background, strong communication skills, and experience with techniques such as patch-clamping, imaging, or molecular biology; send a statement of interest, CV, and three references to Dr. Bo Duan. Graduate students in the MCDB or Neuroscience Graduate Programs may contact the lab about rotations. All undergraduate students are welcome to apply by emailing Dr. Duan directly.
